findings_draft.question: Q1
findings_draft.finding: Forward curve up ~50-70bp at the short end since the July guide (Fed hiked to 4.00% on 2026-09-16, curve now prices Dec + two H1-27 hikes per JPM); BAC 10-Q sensitivity +$0.8B/+100bp short end; JPM raised FY26 NII +$0.7B and NII ex-Markets grew +4.4% QoQ; H.8 deposits +1.6% QoQ. BAC likely lifts NII outlook (FY26 ~8%+, Q4 ~$17B FTE, constructive 2027).

findings_draft.question: Q2
findings_draft.finding: Peers' Q3 capital markets beat the environment BAC pre-guided: JPM IB +14% YoY (DCM +4%, ECM +7%, advisory +32%), GS IB +21%, markets +6% to +15% at JPM/C, GS equities +72%; BAC under-guided Q3 2025 (guided IB ~+10-15%, printed +43%). Consensus ($1.11) anchored on the pre-guide (JPM analyst model at pre-guide inputs gives $1.12).

findings_draft.question: Q4
findings_draft.finding: BA Master Credit Card Trust II NCO rate 2.13% (Jul) and 2.15% (Aug) vs 2.23% (Jun) and 2.39% (Apr); 30+ delinquency flat 1.26-1.28%; JPM's wholesale build was from new activity, WFC provision beat.

findings_draft.question: Q5
findings_draft.finding: AOCI was -$12.0B at June 30 and the analyst expects -$15-16B after the Q3 rate rise; AOCI counts in BAC's CET1 (Category I), the GSIB surcharge is expected to rise on 2027-01-01, and JPM cut its Q3 buyback to $1.06B from $6.7B: BAC's Q3 buyback likely below the $6.0B Q2 pace, possibly more than the street's 'could slow'.
